The cell did complete a short daytime pilot without any interruption, which is encouraging. Before I authorize the overnight run, I need to hear from each of you on readiness. Let's go around the room: training supervision, quality engineering, electrical maintenance — what are your relevant readiness items for this new-cell run?

transcript.text: I need to flag a staffing concern. My roster check found that only one of tonight's three scheduled operators holds the current automated-cell certification. Plant policy requires two certified operators on the cell. The good news is I've confirmed that a certified day-shift operator is available to cover the second position, and I verified all the credentials in the training system this afternoon. However, the overnight roster hasn't been updated yet because system synchronization is still pending. So we can meet the two-certified-operator requirement, but the paperwork won't reflect it until the sync completes.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical item from the customer's release protocol that I reviewed this morning. The protocol — which I received from the customer quality portal — specifies two mandatory requirements before any overnight production can be released: first, the cell's measurement-system check must be completed, and second, the first 50 consecutive inspected parts must pass validation. This protocol has not yet been added to the cell's local startup checklist, so if we're relying solely on that checklist tonight, we'd miss these requirements entirely. I'd recommend we incorporate both items into tonight's startup procedure before Maya authorizes the run.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical electrical issue. During my pre-shift thermal scan of the new inspection cell's control cabinet, I found a loose terminal. This terminal must be repaired before the cell can operate — it's a safety and reliability risk. The repair will take exactly 90 minutes. I recorded the finding in my maintenance notebook, but I want to be transparent that the electronic work order hasn't been opened yet, so it wouldn't show up in the system if anyone checked. We need to factor that 90-minute repair window into the readiness plan before Maya authorizes the overnight run.
